question: Does a compact policy preserve meaning and reduce writing overhead compared with no added policy and the supplied full kit?
primary_gate: No new material semantic or output-contract failure relative to baseline on matched cases. Any failure blocks a quality-superiority claim.
secondary: Blinded task-level ratings for readability and unnecessary overhead; paired output characters, wall seconds and available usage. Shorter is not automatically better.
adoption_rule: Prefer smallest instruction set only if no observed material regression; call this a bounded pilot, never statistical equivalence or reader comprehension proof. Full skill adoption requires independent discovery and workflow tests.
grading: Agent review against frozen invariants; output labels shuffled before first review. No human reader study. Author-agent review is not independent validation.
isolation: Fresh sessions, no memories, no native user skill injection; no tools for content study. Full instructions directly supplied, so file discovery is not measured.
